artworks.title: The Procession of the Trojan Horse into Troy
artworks.description: Tiepolo's horse enters Troy — among the warriors hidden inside, later tradition places Anticlus, whom Odysseus throttles when Helen calls the victims' names and he nearly answers.

artworks.title: The Building of the Trojan Horse
artworks.description: Companion canvas: the hollow timber under construction — the cavity that will hold Anticlus until Odysseus' hand closes his mouth in the night of the sack.

artworks.title: Child Murder (Mykonos Vase, detail)
artworks.description: The Mykonos pithos that first shows the Trojan Horse — the stratagem whose interior silence Anticlus nearly breaks when Helen mimics the Greek wives.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: Konchalovsky's miniseries restages the Wooden Horse and Odysseus' cunning — the night Anticlus' almost-cry belongs to in the epic cycle.

popCulture.title: Odyssey
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: In the Odyssey's horse-tale (and later Little Iliad tradition), Anticlus nearly answers Helen's voice-trick until Odysseus clamps his mouth — the silenced Greek inside the timber.

popCulture.title: Anticlus
popCulture.description: Achaean warrior in the Wooden Horse — remembered for the cry Odysseus stops, not for a separate heroic cycle.
